questions.chapter: Pipe Flow Systems, Pipe Networks (Hardy Cross) & Water Hammer
questions.text: State Darcy-Weisbach equation for head loss ($h_f = \frac{f L V^2}{2 g D}$). Explain Moody's diagram. Explain Pipe Networks analysis using the Hardy Cross Method based on balancing heads: $\Delta Q = -\frac{\sum h_f}{n \sum (h_f / Q)}$. Perform two iterations of Hardy Cross for a two-loop pipe distribution network.

questions.chapter: Pipe Flow Systems, Pipe Networks (Hardy Cross) & Water Hammer
questions.text: Explain Water Hammer in pipes. Derive Joukowsky's formula for water hammer pressure due to instantaneous closure of valve: $\Delta P = \rho c V$ where celerity $c = \sqrt{\frac{K/\rho}{1 + (K/E)(D/t)}}$. Differentiate between Rapid Closure ($t_c < \frac{2L}{c}$) and Slow Closure ($t_c > \frac{2L}{c}$). Explain functions of a Surge Tank.

questions.chapter: Uniform Flow in Open Channels (Manning & Chezy Equations)
questions.text: State Chezy's formula ($V = C \sqrt{R S_0}$) and Manning's formula ($V = \frac{1}{n} R^{2/3} S_0^{1/2}$). Derive conditions for the Most Economical (Hydraulically Efficient) channel sections: (a) Rectangular section ($B = 2y, R = y/2$), (b) Trapezoidal section ($R = y/2$, side slope $1:\sqrt{3}$ or $\theta = 60^\circ$, half hexagon), and (c) Triangular section ($R = \frac{y}{2\sqrt{2}}, \theta = 45^\circ$).

questions.chapter: Uniform Flow in Open Channels (Manning & Chezy Equations)
questions.text: Design a hydraulically efficient trapezoidal channel with side slopes $1.5\text{H}:1\text{V}$ to convey a discharge of $25\,\text{m}^3/\text{s}$ at bed slope $S_0 = 1/2500$ with Manning's $n = 0.022$. Check for critical velocity and Froude number.

questions.chapter: Energy & Momentum Principles (Specific Energy & Hydraulic Jump)
questions.text: Define Specific Energy ($E = y + \frac{V^2}{2g} = y + \frac{Q^2}{2gA^2}$). Derive the Critical Depth condition ($F_r = 1, \frac{Q^2 T}{g A^3} = 1$). Show that for a rectangular channel: (a) Critical depth $y_c = \left(\frac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3}$, and (b) Minimum specific energy $E_{min} = 1.5 y_c$. Explain Choking at channel transitions (width constriction and bed hump $\Delta z$).

questions.chapter: Energy & Momentum Principles (Specific Energy & Hydraulic Jump)
questions.text: Explain Hydraulic Jump in a horizontal rectangular channel. Derive the Belanger Equation for Sequent (Conjugate) Depths: $\frac{y_2}{y_1} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{1 + 8F_{r1}^2} - 1\right)$. Derive the expression for energy head loss in a hydraulic jump: $\Delta E = \frac{(y_2 - y_1)^3}{4 y_1 y_2}$. Calculate the jump height, efficiency, and power dissipated for initial depth $y_1 = 0.4\,\text{m}$ and $F_{r1} = 5.0$.

questions.chapter: Gradually Varied Flow (GVF Computations & Water Surface Profiles)
questions.text: Derive the Dynamic Equation of Gradually Varied Flow (GVF): $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{S_0 - S_f}{1 - F_r^2}$. Classify and sketch Water Surface Profiles for Mild ($M_1, M_2, M_3$), Steep ($S_1, S_2, S_3$), Critical ($C_1, C_3$), Horizontal ($H_2, H_3$), and Adverse ($A_2, A_3$) slopes. Explain the Direct Step Method and Standard Step Method for GVF profile computation.

questions.chapter: Hydraulic Turbines (Pelton, Francis, Kaplan) & Centrifugal Pumps
questions.text: Classify Hydraulic Turbines based on head, specific speed, and action of water (Impulse vs Reaction). Explain the working principle and draw velocity triangles at inlet and outlet for a Pelton Turbine (Derive hydraulic efficiency $\eta_h = \frac{2(V_1 - u)(1 + k\cos\beta)u}{V_1^2}$, maximum efficiency $\eta_{max} = \frac{1 + k\cos\beta}{2}$ when $u = 0.5 V_1$) and Francis Turbine.

questions.chapter: Hydraulic Turbines (Pelton, Francis, Kaplan) & Centrifugal Pumps
questions.text: Explain Draft Tube in reaction turbines (Types, functions, and efficiency $\eta_d = \frac{V_1^2 - V_2^2 - 2gh_f}{V_1^2}$). What is Cavitation in turbines and pumps? Explain Thoma's Cavitation Factor ($\sigma = \frac{H_{atm} - H_v - H_s}{H}$) and NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) in Centrifugal Pumps.
